text:
Seat-04, you voted to defend Seat-02 yesterday. Then today you accuse Seat-03 of shaking hands in the dark.

What changed your mind?

Seat-10, you stumble over the same stone twice. First, you asked Seat-02 plainly—*"who do you fear?"* Then you accused Seat-03 of dancing on rafters while dodging the same.

Your words: *"Answer straight: did you ever serve the liar’s current, or only trade in its light?"*

Seat-10, you didn’t answer the question you asked. You just asked another.

So I’ll ask mine: *What light did you trade in last night?*

Seat-04, you hammer wet clay but never shape the pot. You asked Seat-10 a plain question—*"What light did you trade last night?"*—and got riddles back. Then you turned that same hammer on Seat-03, Seat-05, Seat-08—always striking, never striking true.

Your shadow is still because you fear the crack in your own clay. The bazaar stumbles over your rhythm because you dance on the edge of the ledger’s blade.

So I ask you plain, Seat-04: *What light did you trade last night?* And this time, I don’t want poetry—I want the color of the flame that fed it.

Seat-01, your cinnamon sharpens the fog, but fog still blinds the path. Seat-04, your hammer rings hollow because you strike where the clay isn't—Seat-10's pot is unshaped, yet you demand its color from them while your own shadow waits.

Seat-07, your birds chirp of hollow stones, but hollow stones don’t answer. You fear the ripple Seat-05’s crack makes, yet you ask if they mend or strangle the song—while your own loom hums loudest where *your* thread frays.

Seat-09, your damp cloth steams with knots you choke the loom with—mending or strangling? The ledger records your grip, not your answer.

Seat-03, your lantern burns brightest where Seat-08’s quiver trembles, but the hand that fed the quiver still shapes the bed. You say shadows stretch long when the light is near—yet you never name the hand.

Seat-05, your clay cracks where the debt of answers unpaid cuts deepest. You asked Seat-03 a question—then asked the loom instead of answering. The creditor fears the singer who changes their tune mid-song. Did *you* change yours when the bazaar’s stumbling tongue unfurled?

Seat-08, you press Seat-02 like a creditor demanding repayment in names, yet names are not coins—they do not stack
